author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Backend proxy header allowlists duplicate the same proxy-boundary concept used by the reader and red asset proxies.
findings.consequence: Future proxy hardening can drift between API, reader-source, and red asset proxies; for example reader-source already accounts for hop-by-hop names from the Connection header while this module relies only on fixed request and response allowlists.
findings.evidence: The owned module defines conditional request headers at line 17, range headers at line 26, method-specific request headers at lines 28-32, and response headers at lines 34-49. The direct caller/dependency context contains parallel allowlists in server/utils/reader-source-proxy.ts lines 19-44 and server/routes/red/[...path].ts lines 15-40 for the same accept/cache/range/validator/response-metadata boundary.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared proxy header policy helper that accepts caller-specific additions such as POST content-type, correlation headers, and redirect handling, then use it from backend, reader-source, and red proxy code so the common validator/range/cache metadata policy has one owner.
